body.p: These remarks are responsive to the Office action dated May 16, 2024. Prior to entry of this response, claims 1-19 were pending in the application. By way of this response, claims 1, 12, and 15 are amended, and claims 2 and 14 are cancelled without prejudice. Applicant respectfully requests reconsideration of the application and allowance of the pending claims.
Claims 1 and 12 are objected to because of informalities.
Applicant submits that claims 1 and 12 are hereby amended to address said informalities.
Accordingly, Applicant submits that the objection to claims 1 and 12 should be withdrawn and such action is respectfully requested.
Claims 1-13 and 15-19 rejected under 35 U.S.C. 101 on the asserted basis that the claimed invention is directed to non-statutory subject matter.

Claims 1-6 and 8-19 are rejected under 35 U.S.C. 101 on the asserted basis that the claimed invention is directed to a judicial exception (i.e., a law of nature, a natural phenomenon, or an abstract idea) without significantly more.
Applicant submits that claims 2 and 14 are hereby cancelled, thus rendering moot the 35 U.S.C. 101 rejection thereof.
Applicant traverses the rejection of the remaining claims.

While not believed to be required and solely for the purpose of expediting prosecution of the present application, and further without conceding the merits of the 35 U.S.C. 101 rejection, Applicant submits that independent claim 1 is hereby amended to incorporate features that were previously recited by dependent claim 2, which is hereby cancelled.

Applicant notes that independent claim 1 as hereby amended includes "a threshold monitor arranged to receive the user data and to determine, based at least in part on the user data and at least one threshold value, an active state of the user; and an active time monitor

arranged to receive an indication of the active state from the threshold monitor and to determine, based at least in part on a temporal threshold value, the inference of the cognitive state of the user" (with emphasis added). Consequently, Applicant submits that independent claim 1 as amended is directed to non-statutory subject matter.
Accordingly, Applicant submits that the 35 U.S.C. 101 rejection of claims 1, 3-13, and 16-19 should be withdrawn and such action is respectfully requested.

Applicant submits that independent claim 15 as hereby amended recites features that are substantially similar to features recited by independent claim 1 and, therefore, independent claim 15 should be allowed for at least the same reasons that pertain to independent claim 1.
Accordingly, Applicant submits that the 35 U.S.C. 101 rejection of independent claim 15 should be withdrawn and such action is respectfully requested.

Claim 15 rejected under 35 U.S.C. 112(b) or 35 U.S.C. 112 (pre-AIA), second paragraph, as being indefinite for failing to particularly point out and distinctly claim the subject matter which the inventor or a joint inventor, or for pre-AIA the applicant regards as the invention.
Applicant traverses this rejection.

While not believed to be required and solely for the purpose of expediting prosecution of the present application, and further without conceding the merits of the 35 U.S.C. 112(b) or 35 U.S.C. 112 (pre-AIA), second paragraph, rejection, Applicant submits that independent claim 15 is hereby amended to address the 35 U.S.C. 112(b) or 35 U.S.C. 112 (pre-AIA), second paragraph, rejection thereof.
Accordingly, Applicant submits that the 35 U.S.C. 112(b) or 35 U.S.C. 112 (pre-AIA), second paragraph, rejection of independent claim 15 should be withdrawn and such action is respectfully requested.
Claims 1-9 and 12-18 are rejected under 35 U.S.C. 102(a)(2) as being anticipated by United Kingdom Reference No. GB 2528083 (Popham et al., hereinafter Popham).
Applicant traverses this rejection.
In order for a single prior art reference to anticipate a claim, the reference must teach each and every element recited in the claim. Indeed, MPEP § 2131 specifies that

"[t]he identical invention must be shown in as complete detail as is contained in the claim" (citing Richardson v. Suzuki Motor Co., 868 F.2d 1226, 1236, 9 USPQ2d 1913, 1920 (Fed. Cir. 1989)). Applicant respectfully submits that Popham does not teach each and every element of any of the rejected claims for at least the reasons set forth below.
While not believed to be required and solely for the purpose of expediting prosecution of the present application, and further without conceding the merits of the
35 U.S.C. 102(a)(2) rejection, Applicant submits that independent claim 1 is hereby amended to incorporate features that were previously recited by dependent claim 2, which is hereby cancelled.

Independent claim 1 as hereby amended is directed to a system for determining a cognitive state of a user of a vehicle to control one or more functions of the vehicle, the system being implemented by one or more controllers, and recites the following features (with emphasis added):
one or more inputs for receiving user data from a plurality of
associated user monitoring devices for each monitoring at least one respective attribute of the user of the vehicle, the user data being indicative
of the plurality of respective attributes;
a plurality of inference modules each arranged to receive user data

from one or more of the user monitoring devices, and to each determine a respective inference of a cognitive state of the user based at least in part on the received user data, wherein each of the plurality of inference modules is arranged to output user state data indicative of the determined inference of
the cognitive state of the user; and
an inference fusion module arranged to receive the user state data

from each of the plurality of inference modules, to determine an inference of an aggregated cognitive state of the user and to output cognitive state data indicative of the aggregated cognitive state for controlling the one or
more functions of the vehicle based thereon,

wherein one or more of the plurality of inference modules comprises: a threshold monitor arranged to receive the user data and to determine, based at least in part on the user data and at least one threshold
value, an active state of the user; and

an active time monitor arranged to receive an indication of the active state from the threshold monitor and to determine, based at least in part on a temporal threshold value, the inference of the cognitive state of the user.

Applicant submits that Popham does not teach at least "wherein one or more of the plurality of inference modules comprises: a threshold monitor arranged to receive the user data and to determine, based at least in part on the user data and at least one threshold value, an active state of the user; and an active time monitor arranged to receive an indication of the active state from the threshold monitor and to determine, based at least in part on a temporal threshold value, the inference of the cognitive state of the user," as recited by independent claim 1 as hereby amended. The Office at pages 9-10 of the Office action directs attention to page 9, lines 26-27 and page 10 of Popham as disclosing these features but Applicant notes that the cited portions do not disclose the recited features; rather, these portions of Popham instead merely describe "lower than usual eyelids [that] may be recorded as a fatigued emotion state" and a "monitoring system [that] may assess a higher likelihood or tiredness in the drive emotion state," respectively. Applicant submits that these portions of Popham do not teach the "at least one threshold value" or "active time monitor" recited by the claims.

Because Popham does not teach or suggest every feature recited by independent claim 1, Applicant submits that the 35 U.S.C. 102(a)(2) rejection of independent claim 1 and its dependent claims 2-9 and 16-18 should be withdrawn and such action is respectfully requested. Claims 2-9 and 16-18 are also independently patentable.

Applicant submits that independent claim 15 as hereby amended recites features that are substantially similar to features recited by independent claim 1 and, therefore, independent claim 15 should be allowed for at least the same reasons that pertain to independent claim 1.
Accordingly, Applicant submits that the 35 U.S.C. 102(a)(2) rejection of independent claim 15 should be withdrawn and such action is respectfully requested.
Claims 10, 11, and 19 are rejected under 35 U.S.C. 103 as being unpatentable over Popham in view of U.S. Patent No. 9,977,593 (Ricci).
Applicant traverses this rejection.
Applicant submits that claims 10, 11, and 19 each depend from independent claim 1 and should thus be allowed for at least the same reasons that pertain to the parent claim.
Claims 10, 11, and 19 are also independently patentable. Further, Applicant notes that Ricci fails to cure the deficiencies of Popham.
Accordingly, Applicant submits that the 35 U.S.C. 103 rejection of claims 10, 11, and 19 should be withdrawn and such action is respectfully requested.

Applicant believes that this application is now in condition for allowance, in view of the above amendments and remarks. Accordingly, Applicant respectfully requests that the Examiner issue a Notice of Allowability covering the pending claims. If the Examiner has any questions, or if a telephone interview would in any way advance prosecution of the application, please contact the undersigned attorney of record.
Please charge any cost incurred in the filing of this response, along with any other costs, to Deposit Account No. 601570.
Respectfully submitted,
